introduction: This foundational level introduces Alternative Dispute Resolution (ADR) as a mechanism to resolve disputes outside the traditional, heavily burdened civil court system. It outlines the primary modes of ADR and their statutory integration into the Civil Procedure Code.

core_concepts.title: What is ADR and Section 89 of CPC?
core_concepts.description:
ADR refers to techniques and mechanisms used to resolve disputes without a formal trial in a court of law. 
- Section 89 of CPC: Inserted via the 1999 amendment. It mandates that if the court feels there are elements of a settlement which may be acceptable to the parties, the court SHALL formulate the terms of settlement and refer the dispute to: (1) Arbitration, (2) Conciliation, (3) Judicial Settlement/Lok Adalat, or (4) Mediation.

core_concepts.title: The Big Four ADR Mechanisms
core_concepts.description:
1. Arbitration: A private judge (Arbitrator) hears both sides and passes a legally binding decision (Award).
2. Conciliation: A neutral third party (Conciliator) actively assists parties, suggests solutions, and helps them draft a settlement agreement.
3. Mediation: A neutral third party (Mediator) facilitates communication between parties so they can reach a solution themselves. (The mediator does not impose or suggest solutions).
4. Lok Adalat: 'People's Court'. Organized under the Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987. Focuses on compromise. An award passed by a Lok Adalat has the force of a civil court decree.

core_concepts.title: The Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996
core_concepts.description:
The primary statute governing arbitration in India, completely overhauling the outdated 1940 Act.
- Foundation: It is strictly based on the **UNCITRAL Model Law** (United Nations Commission on International Trade Law), ensuring Indian arbitration aligns with global commercial standards.
- Dual Structure: Part I deals with Domestic Arbitration (arbitration seated in India). Part II deals with the enforcement of Foreign Arbitral Awards (like the New York and Geneva Conventions).

important_entities.name: Binding Nature of ADR Outcomes
important_entities.key_fact: Not all ADR outcomes have immediate legal teeth.
important_entities.significance: An Arbitral Award is immediately binding and enforceable like a court decree. A successful Conciliation settlement agreement also has the status of an arbitral award. However, if Mediation fails, parties simply return to court; the mediator cannot force a decision on them.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Examiners frequently ask: 'A and B orally agree to resolve their contract dispute via arbitration. Is this valid under the 1996 Act?' **NO**. Under Section 7(3) of the Act, an arbitration agreement MUST absolutely be in writing. Oral arbitration agreements hold zero legal validity.

mnemonics_and_tricks.memory_phrase: Mediator = Mute Facilitator; Conciliator = Pro-Active Creator
mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: A mediator just improves communication. A conciliator actively draws up terms of settlement and proposes solutions.

exam_strategy_tips: Whenever a Judiciary question asks 'Which international model forms the basis of the Indian Arbitration Act, 1996?', unconditionally select the **UNCITRAL Model Law**.
